creationPrompt:
Create a weekly planner for me as a Claw Me Page. Include three priorities, a daily reset, friday review. Replace illustrative data, preserve relevant evidence and uncertainty, and check totals or percentages. Ask only for missing information in one concise batch: week, priorities, fixed appointments, energy preferences, available time and review routine.

Use the Claw Me source at https://github.com/clawdotme/plugin in templates/weekly-planner/index.html and templates/_shared/tailwind/README.md. Preserve Archivo, Bitter, the shared theme tokens, and accessible contrast. Author scoped Tailwind 3.4.19 components and compile bundled CSS; do not use a browser CDN. Use semantic responsive HTML, working section links, and useful native details/summary interactions. No scripts, forms, tracking, or embedded frames in the static Page. Deliver matching HTML and PDF from the same content, expand disclosures for print, and inspect page breaks. Use a readable portrait PDF. Keep the result private for review; do not send messages, connect services, purchase anything, or change sharing without my instruction. PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A weekly planner that balances focused work, appointments, and a realistic review.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional independent builder plans around three priorities and leaves space for routine work. The planner is a snapshot to discuss and update, not an automatic calendar integration.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Day: Monday · Main focus: Write project brief · Fixed commitment: Team check-in · Buffer: One hour
Day: Tuesday · Main focus: Build first example · Fixed commitment: None · Buffer: Two hours
Day: Wednesday · Main focus: Review with client · Fixed commitment: 14:00 review · Buffer: One hour
Day: Thursday · Main focus: Apply agreed changes · Fixed commitment: None · Buffer: Two hours
Day: Friday · Main focus: Handover and reflection · Fixed commitment: Weekly close · Buffer: One hour
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Three priorities: Finish the brief, review a working example, and hand over the agreed result. New work should be compared with those commitments before it is added to the week.
A daily reset: At the end of each day, record what actually moved and the next useful step. Carry unfinished work forward deliberately rather than copying an entire unchecked list.
Friday review: What was completed, what changed, and what should stop? Use the answers to plan the next week. The aim is a credible schedule, not a perfect record of busyness.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: planner layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
